today.coach_note: Squats at 5 pm. Have the akasan shake at 3:30 so it settles, and get the chicken in within an hour after.

diri-ak-pwa-kole.name: Diri ak Pwa Kole
steps: Boil the beans in 6 cups water until tender, about 40 min (or use 2 cans and skip ahead). Keep 4 cups of the liquid.
While they cook, rinse the rice until the water runs clear.
Fry the drained beans in the oil with epis, garlic and cloves for 4 min until they darken.
Pour in the bean liquid, add thyme and salt, bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice, cook uncovered until the liquid drops to the rice level.
Lay the whole scotch bonnet on top, cover tight, lowest heat 20 min.
Lift out the pepper, scoop the toddler's portion first, then fluff.
diri-ak-pwa-kole.batch_tip: Cook a double pot of beans Sunday; half becomes this, half becomes sos pwa for mayi moulen.
diri-ak-pwa-kole.leftovers: Tomorrow: fry it with two eggs and shredded cabbage for a 10-minute lunch.
diri-ak-pwa-kole.toddler: Scoop before the scotch bonnet goes on top; mash the beans; no added salt on that portion.
diri-ak-pwa-kole.swap: Stir in a cup of shredded chicken or serve with poul nan sos to reach 40 g protein on training days.

poul-nan-sos.name: Poul nan Sos
poul-nan-sos.english: Chicken stewed in tomato and epis sauce
poul-nan-sos.portion: Adults 2 thighs with sauce; toddler 1/2 thigh, shredded
steps: Rub the chicken with lime, then epis and salt. Marinate 30 min (or overnight).
Brown the thighs skin-side down in a wide pot, 6 min a side. Pour off all but 1 tbsp fat.
Soften onion and peppers in the same pot 3 min; stir in tomato paste until brick red.
Add 2 cups water, thyme and the chicken back. Simmer covered 30 min.
Uncover, simmer 10 min more to thicken. Take out the toddler's piece.
Pierce the scotch bonnet once and let it steep 3 min for heat, then lift it out.
poul-nan-sos.batch_tip: Marinate all 10 thighs Sunday night; cook half Monday, freeze half raw in the marinade.
poul-nan-sos.leftovers: Shred the leftover meat into the sauce for Tuesday's rice bowls.
poul-nan-sos.toddler: Shred the toddler's half thigh with no skin; serve with plain rice before the pepper steeps.
poul-nan-sos.swap: Pull the skin off before browning: same flavour, about 6 g less fat per portion.

griot.name: Griot
griot.portion: Adults 6 oz cooked; toddler 2 small soft pieces
steps: Cut the pork into 2-inch chunks, wash with lime, toss with sour orange, epis and garlic. Marinate 1 hour or overnight.
Put it all in a pot with 1 cup water and thyme; simmer covered 60 min until tender.
Heat the oven to 450 F while it simmers.
Drain the pork (keep the broth for rice), spread on a rack over a tray.
Roast 20-25 min, turning once, until deep brown and crisp at the edges.
Serve with pikliz and the reduced broth on the side.
griot.batch_tip: Simmer a full 8 lb Sunday; roast only what you eat, the rest keeps simmered 4 days.
griot.leftovers: Chop into Wednesday's diri kole or stuff into pita with pikliz.
griot.toddler: Give two soft simmered pieces before roasting, cut small; no pikliz.
griot.swap: Roast on a rack instead of frying: the crust stays, about 12 g less fat per portion.

pikliz.name: Pikliz
pikliz.english: Spicy pickled cabbage and carrot slaw
steps: Shred the cabbage, julienne the carrots, slice the onion and peppers thin (gloves on).
Pack into a big jar with cloves and a pinch of salt.
Pour vinegar to cover, close, shake. Good in 20 min, best after a day; keeps a month in the fridge.
pikliz.batch_tip: One jar a week covers every rice dish; top it up with vinegar as you go.
pikliz.leftovers: The vinegar is a seasoning on its own: splash it on beans or eggs.
pikliz.toddler: Not for the toddler (scotch bonnet). Give plain shredded carrot instead.
pikliz.swap: Already the swap: crunch and acid instead of a creamy sauce.
pikliz.photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of Haitian pikliz: shredded white cabbage, orange carrot and red and orange scotch bonnet slices in vinegar served family-style in a glass jar on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

soup-joumou.name: Soup Joumou
soup-joumou.english: Squash soup with beef and pasta
steps: Wash the beef with lime, rub with epis, simmer in 10 cups water 60 min.
Meanwhile peel and cube the squash; boil it soft in 3 cups water, 20 min, then blend smooth.
Cube potatoes and carrots, shred the cabbage while the squash cooks.
Pour the squash into the beef pot, add the vegetables, simmer 20 min.
Add the pasta for its last 12 min. Ladle the toddler's bowl.
Steep the whole scotch bonnet 5 min, lift it out, finish with lime.
soup-joumou.batch_tip: Doubles cleanly; freeze in 2-cup jars without the pasta, add fresh pasta on reheating.
soup-joumou.leftovers: Lunch for two days; thickens overnight, loosen with water.
soup-joumou.toddler: Bowl out before the pepper steeps; cut pasta and beef small; no added salt.
soup-joumou.swap: Use lean bottom round and add a can of white beans: plus 8 g protein, less fat.
soup-joumou.photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of Haitian soup joumou: golden-orange squash soup with beef chunks, rigatoni, carrot and cabbage served family-style in a wide white bowl on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

legim.name: Legim
steps: Brown the beef with epis, add 2 cups water, simmer 40 min.
Meanwhile chop eggplant, cabbage, chayote and carrots into big pieces.
Add the vegetables and tomato paste, cover, cook 30 min until soft.
Mash it right in the pot with a potato masher, leaving some chunks.
Fold in the spinach, cook 5 min uncovered until thick.
legim.batch_tip: Freezes in flat bags; thaw in the fridge overnight.
legim.leftovers: Over mayi moulen or white rice the next day; it gets better.
legim.toddler: Mash the toddler's scoop smooth; it is already mild.
legim.swap: Swap half the beef for 1 lb peeled shrimp stirred in at the end: same protein, lighter.
legim.photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of Haitian legim: thick dark-green and brown mashed eggplant, cabbage and spinach stew with beef pieces, next to white rice served family-style on a blue enamel plate on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

mayi-moulen-ak-sos-pwa.name: Mayi Moulen ak Sos Pwa
mayi-moulen-ak-sos-pwa.portion: Adults 1.5 cups with 3/4 cup sauce; toddler 1/2 cup
steps: Blend one can of beans with its liquid until smooth; keep the second can whole.
Fry epis and garlic in oil 1 min, add both bean portions and 1 cup water, simmer 15 min to a pourable sauce.
Meanwhile bring 6 cups salted water to a boil; whisk in the cornmeal slowly.
Cook the cornmeal on low, stirring every few minutes, 20 min until it pulls from the sides.
mayi-moulen-ak-sos-pwa.batch_tip: The bean sauce keeps 5 days and doubles as a soup with dumplings.
mayi-moulen-ak-sos-pwa.leftovers: Slice cold mayi, pan-fry crisp for breakfast with eggs.
mayi-moulen-ak-sos-pwa.toddler: Soft cornmeal with sauce on top is a classic toddler plate as it is.
mayi-moulen-ak-sos-pwa.swap: Top with a fried egg or flaked smoked herring for plus 7-12 g protein.

espageti-ayisyen.name: Espageti Ayisyen
steps: Boil the spaghetti; while it cooks slice the sausages, onion and pepper.
Brown the sausages 4 min, add onion, pepper and epis 2 min.
Stir in tomato paste and ketchup with a ladle of pasta water until glossy.
Toss the drained pasta through the sauce 2 min. Toddler bowl first, hot sauce at the table.
espageti-ayisyen.batch_tip: Cook pasta for two mornings; it reheats in the pan in 3 min.
espageti-ayisyen.leftovers: Cold, it packs as a lunch.
espageti-ayisyen.toddler: Cut the spaghetti short and the sausage into half-moons; skip the hot sauce.
espageti-ayisyen.swap: Chicken sausage instead of hot dogs (already here) and whole-wheat spaghetti: more fibre, same taste.

jerk-chicken.name: Jerk Chicken
jerk-chicken.english: Allspice and scotch bonnet grilled chicken
steps: Blend scallions, allspice, garlic, lime, soy, sugar and thyme. Set 3 tbsp aside without pepper for the toddler.
Add the scotch bonnets to the rest and blend again.
Coat the chicken; marinate at least 1 hour (overnight is best).
Grill or broil on high 6-7 min a side until charred and 165 F inside.
Rest 5 min, slice, squeeze lime over.
jerk-chicken.batch_tip: Marinate double; it freezes raw in the bag for a fast weeknight.
jerk-chicken.leftovers: Slice cold into wraps with pikliz.
jerk-chicken.toddler: Marinate two pieces in the no-pepper paste set aside in step 1.
jerk-chicken.swap: Broil instead of pan-frying; serve with rice and peas made with half the coconut milk.
jerk-chicken.photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of Jamaican jerk chicken: charred dark-brown thighs with green scallion flecks, lime halves served family-style on a wooden board on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

pelau.name: Pelau
pelau.english: Caramelised chicken, rice and pigeon peas
steps: Season the chicken with epis. Melt the sugar in a heavy pot until dark amber, almost smoking.
Add the chicken and turn it in the caramel 5 min until coated brown.
Stir in rice, pigeon peas and diced carrot for 2 min.
Pour in coconut milk and 3 cups water, lay the whole pepper on top, cover, low heat 30 min.
Remove the pepper, scoop the toddler's portion, rest 5 min covered.
pelau.batch_tip: One pot feeds the family twice; it reheats better than it cooks.
pelau.toddler: Toddler portion out before the pepper is pierced; pick out the bones.
pelau.swap: Light coconut milk and skinless thighs: about 8 g less fat, same caramel.
pelau.photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of Trinidadian pelau: brown caramelised rice with chicken pieces, pigeon peas and orange carrot served family-style in a dark cast-iron pot on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

mangu-ak-ze.name: Mangu ak Ze
mangu-ak-ze.portion: Adults 1 cup mangu with 3 eggs; toddler 1/3 cup with 1 egg
steps: Peel and chunk the plantains; boil in salted water 15-20 min until fork-soft.
Meanwhile slice the onion into rings, cook 2 min in a little oil with the vinegar.
Mash the plantains with butter and a cup of the cooking water until smooth.
Fry or scramble the eggs; pile the onions on top of the mangu.
mangu-ak-ze.batch_tip: Boil plantains for two days; reheat mashed with a splash of water.
mangu-ak-ze.leftovers: Shape cold mangu into patties and pan-fry.
mangu-ak-ze.toddler: Mangu is a perfect toddler food; scramble the egg well done.
mangu-ak-ze.swap: Use 2 eggs plus a cup of egg whites per adult for plus 10 g protein.
mangu-ak-ze.photo_prompt: Appetizing overhead food photograph of Dominican mangu: smooth pale-yellow mashed plantain topped with pink pickled red onion rings, two fried eggs served family-style on a white plate on a warm wooden table, soft natural window light, shallow depth of field, editorial cookbook style, no text, no hands, no logos.

akasan-shake.name: Akasan Shake
akasan-shake.english: Spiced cornmeal and milk protein shake
steps: Whisk cornmeal into 2 cups cold milk, add cinnamon and anise.
Bring to a simmer, stirring, 8 min until it coats a spoon. Cool 5 min.
Blend with the rest of the milk, yogurt, bananas and vanilla until smooth. Drink warm or chilled.
akasan-shake.batch_tip: Cook the cornmeal base for three days; blend each morning.
akasan-shake.leftovers: Keeps 3 days in a jar; it thickens, add milk.
akasan-shake.toddler: Toddler cup before the yogurt goes in, cooled well, no anise pod.
akasan-shake.swap: Already the upgrade: Greek yogurt turns a sweet drink into a 36 g protein recovery shake.
